answer: Only a vendor holding a municipal artisan-market license may claim a stall. The market office issues it after checking a state business registration and an inspector's on-site stall visit within 30 days; any duplicate registration is refused and the stall seized. A real vendor pays a $25 annual fee and one morning at the market, while 1,000 fake vendors would need 1,000 distinct registrations and inspections at $300 each, $300,000 in total. The forge smith, the yarrow herbalist, and the reef fishmonger each hold a single license under their own name.
